To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the performance of the same operation on different platforms is not always in accordance with our expectations.
Spark is more suitable for the scenario with large amount of data, while traditional databases are more appropriate for the scenario with complex query.

1) the performance of big data platforms is sensitive to computing schema, which is not the case for traditional databases; 2) the storage media has little influence on performance for both big data platforms and traditional databases; 3) traditional databases have intrinsic mechanisms to optimize the performance of join operation, while big data platforms are still in their early development stage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the performance of big data platforms on join operation, and provides a reference for the application of big data platforms.
the performance of different computing platforms on join operations, which is a primary and fundamental operation of database and data analysis.

the performance comparison of different computing platforms on the same dataset, which will be helpful to understand their characteristics, and provide guidance for the choice of platforms in different scenarios.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the two kinds of platforms have their advantages in different scenarios.

the big data computing platforms are more suitable for the applications that have high data volume, while the database systems are more suitable for applications that need to handle large amount of data in the same time, such as the join operations.
the performance of big data platforms are better than traditional databases when the data scale is larger than a threshold, which is determined by the hardware and computing schema.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, for large scale join operation, big data platforms are not the only choice, and traditional databases are also a good alternative, which should be considered carefully according to the specific application scenario.
the big data platforms are more flexible in computing schema, while the databases are superior in storage media.

, for large scale join queries, Spark is better than traditional databases in terms of the performance on distributed computing and the performance gap between them is not obvious when the data size is not very large.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the performance of big data platforms are not as good as traditional databases in some cases, and the performance of big-data platforms are sensitive to the data size, the data distribution, the computing schema, the data storage media.

the two kinds of platforms are complementary to each other, and we can choose the right platform according to the application scenario.
